sources.title: Sahara Solar Cooperative Agreement
sources.author: North African Energy Alliance
sources.excerpt: The Sahara Desert now powers half of Europe through vast solar collection arrays.
sources.longExcerpt: What was once the great barrier is now the great provider. Solar panels stretch across the Sahara, drinking sunlight, converting it to electricity that flows through superconducting cables beneath the Mediterranean. Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt - once divided by colonial borders - now united in the Solar Cooperative. Desert communities manage the arrays, their children study engineering, their cities bloom with desalinated water. The sun that once oppressed now liberates.
